text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: the items are the same, but they are easier to find and use. The main goal is to make the code more readable and simpler for other developers (or your future self) to understand. By breaking down long functions and removing duplication, you reduce "technical debt" – the hidden cost of rushed, messy work. While refactoring takes extra time upfront, it saves time later because bugs are easier to spot and features are easier to add. In short, clean code is happier code.
